title: Glowing footprints share the credit
allegory: Eligibility traces are like footprints that glow when you step on them and fade with every step after, so when a surprise comes, every footprint is credited in proportion to how brightly it still glows.
map: how brightly that footprint still glows
every glow fading a little with each step
a surprise, better or worse than expected
the TD error δ = r + γQ(s′, a′) − Q(s, a)
every footprint credited by its glow
Q(s, a) += α·δ·e(s, a) for all pairs at once

cap.1: You walk a long path and find treasure at the end. Who deserves credit? Plain SARSA only credits the very last step, so the news creeps back slowly.
cap.2: One-step SARSA updates only the state-action just before a reward. Credit for a long path takes many episodes to flow back, one step per visit.
cap.3: One-step TD backups move information one transition per update, so long-horizon credit assignment is slow; Monte Carlo returns propagate fast but are high-variance.

cap.1: Picture every footprint glowing as you step on it, then fading. When a surprise comes, every footprint gets credit in proportion to how brightly it still glows.
cap.2: Each state-action pair gets an eligibility trace: bumped when visited, decaying every step. A TD error then updates every pair at once, scaled by its trace.
cap.3: The backward view of TD(λ): traces record recency-weighted visitation, and each TD error δ is broadcast to all pairs with weight e(s, a). Recent and frequent pairs get most credit.

cap.1: Each step: every footprint moves by the surprise times its glow. Then every glow dims by the same factor. λ sets how slowly footprints fade.
cap.2: δ = r + γQ(s′, a′) − Q(s, a), exactly as in SARSA. Every pair updates by α·δ·e, then all traces shrink by γλ. The current pair's trace is bumped before the update.
cap.3: SARSA(λ): increment e(s_t, a_t) (accumulating) or set it to 1 (replacing); Q ← Q + αδe over all pairs; e ← γλe. Traces reset to zero at the start of each episode.

cap.1: How much credit a footprint k steps back gets. Small λ: only the last few steps. Big λ: a long trail. λ = 0 is plain SARSA: the last step alone.
cap.2: Trace weight decays as (γλ)^k with k steps back (here γ = 1). λ = 0 recovers one-step SARSA; λ near 1 approaches Monte Carlo, crediting the whole episode.
cap.3: λ interpolates TD(0) and Monte Carlo: the λ-return weights n-step returns by (1 − λ)λ^(n−1). Small λ: more bootstrap bias, less variance; large λ: the reverse.

chapters.name: Trust guesses or outcomes?
chapters.verdict: GAE's λ in PPO is the same dial.

cap.1: Small λ trusts your own guesses about the future: steady but possibly wrong. Large λ trusts what actually happened: honest but noisy. You pick the balance.
cap.2: Low λ leans on bootstrapped estimates (biased, low variance); high λ leans on observed returns (unbiased, high variance). GAE's λ plays the same role in policy gradients.
cap.3: The trace decay sets an explicit bias/variance trade-off in the target. GAE weights k-step advantage estimates by the same geometric scheme, which is why PPO has a λ setting too.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: The same λ returns in GAE and PPO
Credit assignment shapes what gets learned

cap.1: Deciding which past choices earned a reward is the core puzzle of learning from experience. Fading trails are one elegant answer.
cap.2: You'll meet λ again in GAE, which PPO uses to estimate advantages. Understanding the trace here makes that λ obvious later.
cap.3: Credit assignment decides which behaviour RL reinforces. When you study RL-trained models, γ and λ shaped which earlier actions got credit, and so what the model learned to do.

coda.title: Treasure at step 8: how far back does the credit reach?

caption.1: Drag λ and watch how far back the credit reaches when the treasure appears at step 8. At λ = 0 only the last step learns anything.
caption.2: Bars are the traces when the reward arrives: (γλ)^k for a step k moves back. λ = 0 is one-step SARSA; λ = 1 with γ = 1 credits the whole trail equally, like Monte Carlo.
caption.3: With no revisits, e = (γλ)^k at k steps back, so the effective trace length is about 1/(1 − γλ): the same horizon arithmetic as discounting, applied to credit.

where_else: GAE's λ in PPO: the same bias/variance dial, applied to advantages
Exponential moving averages, such as momentum in Adam: the same fading weights on the past

hamming.what: A decaying record of recently visited state-action pairs, so each TD error updates a whole trail of past choices rather than just the last.
hamming.when: When rewards arrive long after the actions that earned them and one-step updates pass credit back too slowly.
hamming.why: λ dials between one-step TD (steady, biased) and Monte Carlo (unbiased, noisy), and the same dial reappears as GAE's λ in PPO.

object.title: The fading-trail landscape
object.subtitle: Credit left on a footprint, by how many steps back it is and by λ.

cap.1: A landscape of fading credit: left to right is how many steps back a footprint is, front to back is λ, and height is how much credit it still gets.
cap.2: Surface of trace weight (γλ)^k over steps back k and λ.
cap.3: e(k; λ) = (γλ)^k: the whole SARSA(λ) family in one surface.

cap.1: Along the λ = 0 edge there's a single spike: only the newest step gets credit. That edge is plain SARSA.
cap.2: λ = 0: traces vanish after one step, recovering one-step SARSA.
cap.3: At λ = 0 the backward view reduces to the TD(0) update on the current pair.

cap.1: Along the λ = 1 edge, with no discount, the ridge stays flat: every step in the episode gets full credit, like Monte Carlo.
cap.2: λ = 1 and γ = 1: no decay, the whole trail is updated equally.
cap.3: λ → 1 approaches Monte Carlo targets: unbiased but high variance.

cap.1: Add discounting and even the λ = 1 edge fades: traces shrink by γλ every step.
cap.2: With γ = 0.9 every row decays, including λ = 1.
cap.3: The per-step decay is the product γλ, so discounting shortens the trace even at λ = 1.

cap.1: From above, every λ in between makes its own exponential slope. Choosing λ is choosing how long your memory is.
cap.2: Intermediate λ values trade bias against variance by trace length.
cap.3: Effective trace length ≈ 1/(1 − γλ) steps: the dial between bootstrapping and full returns.

predict.q: λ = 0.5, γ = 1. How much trace does a footprint 3 steps back have, visited once?
Which λ turns SARSA(λ) back into plain one-step SARSA?
predict.why: Traces vanish after one step, so only the current pair is updated.

predict.q: Raising λ usually trades what for what?
predict.why: High λ leans on actual returns (unbiased, noisy); low λ leans on bootstrapped estimates (biased, steady).

object.where: Anywhere credit must reach back in time: GAE in PPO, TD(λ) critics, any exponentially fading average.
